checks.statement: Conjugation sends a map fixing t to a map fixing t′=i(g)(t), and retains its projected gamma when i(g) lies in the kernel.
checks.reasoning: Put A=i(g) and f=q_t(gamma). From t′=A(t) and f(t)=t, (AfA^{-1})(t′)=A f(t)=A(t)=t′. With p(A)=1 from the displayed kernel role, p(AfA^{-1})=p(f)=gamma.
checks.outcome: The two defining conditions are compatible with the claimed conjugation formula under these stated hypotheses. This calculation does not prove an unclear subscript is t; the ink remains b|t at C10.

checks.statement: The NB claim that +1 and −1 coincide when n=2.
checks.reasoning: Their difference is 2, so +1≡−1 modulo n exactly when n divides 2. Thus the displayed n=2 example is correct, and the final n≥3 assumption makes the two signs distinct. If positive n=1 were allowed, they would also coincide; the nearby n≠2 parenthesis alone does not state n≥3.
checks.outcome: Confirmed the written n=2 statement and the later n≥3 distinction. Preserved the earlier written n≠2 condition without silently strengthening it.
